entities.summary:
Latino Malabranca Orsini was a Roman noble and Italian cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, born into the esteemed House of Orsini, and serving as nephew of Pope Nicholas III. He held the position of cardinal from 1279 until his death in 1294. Orsini's cause for beatification remains in preliminary stages, despite his reverence within the Order of Preachers. The close ties between the Orsini family and the papacy played a significant role in shaping Italian politics during the late Middle Ages.

As a prominent figure in the Holy Roman Church, Orsini's influence extended beyond the Vatican, with connections to various European monarchies and nobility. His involvement in ecclesiastical politics and diplomacy underscores the intricate web of relationships within the medieval Christian world.

The legacy of Latino Malabranca Orsini can be seen in the continued significance of the Orsini family throughout Italian history, with many notable figures emerging from this lineage. The Orsini's enduring influence also highlights the complex relationships between the Catholic Church and the Italian state during the Middle Ages.

Despite the passing of centuries, the significance of Orsini's life and legacy remains, serving as a testament to the enduring power of the Holy Roman Church and the intricate web of alliances that defined medieval Italy.
